record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.context_brief: Invariant measures for large algebraic group actions
record.original_question: For either a large subgroup Γ of the automorphism group of a finite-volume nilmanifold, or a large subgroup Γ of a Lie group acting by translations on G/Λ where Λ is a lattice in G, are the only ergodic Γ-invariant probability measures those supported on finite Γ-orbits and Haar measure?

evidence.quote: CONJECTURE 14 (A. Furman). Consider one of the following actions of a group Γ: 1. Γ is a “large” (e.g., Zariski dense) subgroup of the group of au tomorphisms of a nilmanifold of ﬁnite volume. 2. Γ is a “large” subgroup of a Lie group acting by translations on G/Λ, where Λ is a lattice in G. Then the only ergodic Γ-invariant probability measures are the measures sup-ported on ﬁnite Γ-orbits and the Haar measure.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ be a group acting by measure-preserving transformations in one of the following two settings:

(1) $N$ is a connected, simply connected nilpotent Lie group, $\Lambda \subset N$ is a lattice (so that $N/\Lambda$ is a finite-volume nilmanifold), and $\Gamma$ is a "large" (for instance, Zariski dense in the real algebraic group $\mathrm{Aut}(N)$) subgroup of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(N/\Lambda)$ of the nilmanifold.

(2) $G$ is a Lie group, $\Lambda \subset G$ is a lattice, and $\Gamma$ is a "large" subgroup of $G$ (for instance, generating a Zariski dense subgroup with sufficient unipotent structure) acting on $G/\Lambda$ by left translations.

Prove or disprove: in either setting, every ergodic $\Gamma$-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu$ on the relevant homogeneous space is either
(a) supported on a finite $\Gamma$-orbit, or
(b) the normalized Haar (Lebesgue) measure on the whole space.
artifact.category_tag: Measure rigidity for group actions on homogeneous spaces
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (attributed to A. Furman) is a measure-rigidity statement that remains open in full generality. Significant partial results exist: for higher-rank abelian actions by toral/nilmanifold automorphisms there are classification theorems under additional hypotheses (positive entropy, TNS conditions, irreducibility) by Katok–Spatzier, Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss, and others; for translation actions, Ratner's theorems handle the case where Γ is generated by unipotents, and recent work of Eskin–Lindenstrauss and Benoist–Quint covers stationary measures under semisimplicity assumptions. Nevertheless, the general Zariski-dense automorphism case (without entropy assumptions) and many translation cases remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Multi-invariant measures and subsets on nilmanifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of ergodic invariant measures for higher-rank abelian actions by nilmanifold automorphisms under TNS/diagonalizability hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Partial measure-classification results are known for higher-rank abelian actions under additional hypotheses, but not in the full Zariski-dense generality.

status_evidence.title: Density of finitely supported invariant measures for automorphisms of compact abelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies ergodic invariant measures for large automorphism groups of compact abelian groups; finite-orbit measures form a dense set.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address the conjecture in special cases, indicating it is not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Invariant Measures for Large Automorphism Groups of Projective Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates analogous measure-rigidity statements for large automorphism group actions.
status_evidence.claim: The general measure rigidity conjecture for large automorphism group actions is an active area with partial results.
